VELoop Rewards 
Tap & Earn — Complete MERN Full-Stack 
Intern Task 
Production-oriented implementation specification 
 
Project VELoop Rewards — Tap & Earn 
Stack MERN: MongoDB + Express.js + React.js + Node.js 
Platform body color #161827 
Primary visual direction Minimal • Premium • Fintech • Interactive • Trusted 
Reference 
Uploaded Tap & Earn concept + uploaded Tap League 
screenshots 
Primary objective 
Build the complete frontend + backend, not a static UI 
demo 
 
1. Task Objective 
Build the complete VELoop Rewards Tap & Earn module as a production-style MERN feature. The experience must feel 
engaging like a modern tap-to-earn game, but the visual language must remain premium, minimal, trustworthy and 
fintech-oriented. The implementation must include real backend state, server-authoritative reward calculation, secure 
tap processing, upgrade systems, seasonal progression, Tap League ranking, reward history and all required UI 
interactions. 
2. Non-Negotiable Requirements 
 Use MERN stack throughout the feature. 
 Frontend must be React.js and responsive for desktop and mobile. 
 Backend must be Node.js + Express.js with MongoDB persistence. 
 Do not hard-code balances, energy, rank, reward history, upgrades or season data in React. 
 Backend is the source of truth for rewards, balances, energy, cooldowns, upgrades and leaderboard scores. 
 Every accepted tap must respect a 200 ms minimum processing interval. Frontend must visibly animate every tap 
and provide vibration feedback where supported. 
 The 200 ms delay must NOT be the only anti-bot mechanism. Backend must reject impossible tap rates and 
suspicious sequences. 
 The UI must never feel cluttered. Advanced features should be understandable at first glance and expandable 
through drawers/modals. 
 Use the supplied Tap & Earn visual concept as the structural inspiration, but do not copy another game's branding 
or assets. 
 Use the platform body color #161827 as the foundation of the design system. 
3. Core Tap Interaction 
The central interaction is the VE coin/tap circle. Every tap must feel responsive even though reward processing is 
controlled by the backend. 

Requirement Implementation 
Tap animation 
Scale/press effect, glow/ripple, small coin/token burst 
and subtle counter animation. 
Haptic feedback 
Use navigator.vibrate where supported; fail silently on 
unsupported devices. 
200 ms interval 
Do not accept another tap event locally until the 200 ms 
interaction window is respected. 
Server authority 
Client sends tap request; server validates state and 
decides reward. 
Reward feedback 
Show a compact floating reward such as +1 SVE, +1.2 VE, 
+25 Tokens or +1 Spin. 
No guaranteed reward per tap 
The tap animation happens on every accepted tap, but 
reward outcomes follow configured reward probabilities. 
Low-latency feel 
Animate immediately; reconcile balance/energy with the 
server response. 
Failed tap 
Show subtle feedback such as 'Too fast' or 'Energy 
empty' without a disruptive modal. 
 
4. Tap Reward Distribution 
Use the following initial reward distribution. These values must be configurable from the backend so the economy can 
be tuned later without changing frontend code. 
Outcome Initial probability Reward range / rule 
SVE 60% 
1 SVE per rewarded SVE outcome 
(initial configuration) 
VE 20% 0.6 to 1.7 VE 
Spin 2% 
1 spin whenever a spin outcome is 
selected 
Gems 5% 0.5, 0.8, 1, 1.2, up to 2 gems 
Tokens 13% remainder 5 to 100 tokens 
 
Important: the listed percentages total 87% before the token remainder. Therefore the backend should define Tokens 
as the remaining 13% so the distribution totals exactly 100%. Do not create an unaccounted reward bucket. 
Reward probabilities must be server-side configuration. The client must never decide whether a tap gives SVE, VE, Spin, 
Gems or Tokens. 
5. Energy System 
Feature Requirement 
Base energy 500 / 500 
Consumption 
1 energy per accepted tap before any efficiency rules are 
applied. 
Recharge +20 energy every 20 minutes by default. 
Storage upgrade User can increase maximum capacity by spending VEs. 
Recharge-speed upgrade 
User can increase recharge speed using the designated 
upgrade currency/tokens. 
Zero energy 
Disable accepted taps until energy becomes available or 
the user uses an eligible recovery option. 
Server calculation 
Energy regeneration must be calculated from 
timestamps rather than requiring a request every 20 
minutes. 

Cap 
Regenerated energy can never exceed maximum storage 
capacity. 
 
6. Energy Storage Capacity 
Default capacity is 500. Users can purchase higher capacity. The exact pricing curve should be configurable. Upgrade 
prices must increase faster than capacity so users cannot create uncontrolled reward inflation. 
Suggested initial progression: 500 → 600 → 700 → 800 → 900 → 1000. Keep the values configurable. 
7. Multitap 
Multitap increases the reward value of an accepted physical tap. Default is x1. Users may upgrade up to x3. The upgrade 
is temporary and remains valid for 7 days from activation/purchase. 
Level Tap effect Validity 
x1 1x Default 
x2 2x 7 days 
x3 3x 7 days 
 
The backend must store activation time and expiry time. After expiry, the user automatically falls back to the highest 
non-expired multiplier. 
8. Recharge Speed 
Users can upgrade energy recharge speed. Keep the upgrade curve configurable. Do not allow recharge speed to 
become unlimited. Suggested initial display: +20/20m → +22/20m → +24/20m → +27/20m → +30/20m. 
9. Tap Streak 
Show the user's current consecutive tap streak. The streak is primarily an engagement mechanic. Use a visible counter 
and a lightweight progress effect. Do not make streak rewards large enough to damage the economy. 
10. Precision Tap 
Occasionally display a small precision target during the tap interaction. A user who taps the target accurately receives 
Tokens. The reward amount should be configured by the backend. Precision taps must not bypass normal energy or 
server validation. 
11. Mystery Tap 
A mystery tap is a special tap outcome that awards SVEs. It should be visually distinct but not excessively flashy. The 
backend decides when the event is available and the reward amount. 

12. Tap Combo 
Tap Combo is an animation/engagement layer. It should visually show the user that they are tapping continuously, for 
example COMBO x12, COMBO x25, COMBO x50. The combo animation itself does not need to create a separate 
economic reward unless explicitly enabled later. 
13. Boost Windows 
Provide a temporary 30-second boost window. The boost may increase the tap reward according to backend 
configuration. It should have a clear countdown, active state and expiry animation. Boost activation must be logged. 
14. Lucky Tap + Spin 
Lucky Tap cannot trigger before the user reaches a minimum of 300 accepted taps in the relevant tracking window. 
After 300 taps, the backend may randomly trigger a Lucky Tap. The reward interaction is a Spin. 
 Show a clear progress indicator toward the 300-tap threshold. 
 Before 300 taps, do not display a misleading 'almost lucky' state that implies a guaranteed reward. 
 After eligibility, the backend controls the trigger. 
 Spin result must be server-generated and recorded in reward history. 
 Prevent double-spinning through idempotent server-side processing. 
15. Tap Missions 
Create daily/seasonal missions that award Tokens. Examples: 
 Complete 100 accepted taps. 
 Complete 500 accepted taps. 
 Reach a target combo. 
 Complete a precision tap. 
 Use a boost window. 
 Return and tap on multiple sessions. 
16. Daily Tap Challenge 
Create a daily challenge with convenient, controlled rewards. The user should see progress immediately. The challenge 
resets according to the platform's daily reset time. Backend must enforce completion and prevent duplicate claims. 
17. Energy Bank 
Users can purchase an Energy Bank valid for 3 days. The Energy Bank is a separate temporary energy reserve. The exact 
capacity and price should be configurable. The UI must clearly show its expiry countdown and remaining capacity. 
18. Energy Shield 
Users can purchase/activate an Energy Shield using SVEs. Shield duration is 10 seconds. During the active window, 
eligible taps do not consume energy. The shield must have a visible countdown and server-side start/expiry 
timestamps. 

19. Tap Efficiency 
Tap Efficiency is a temporary seasonal/monthly upgrade. Initial levels: 1.1x, 1.2x and 1.3x. The user's purchased 
efficiency expires when the current Tap Season expires. Do not make it permanent. 
The frontend must show the current efficiency, current level, upgrade cost and exact expiry date/time. 
20. VE Fragments 
Introduce VE Fragments as a separate collectible/progression resource. The conversion/value will remain configurable 
and can be decided later. Build the data model and UI so the value can change without a database migration. 
21. Tap Seasons 
A Tap Season is a fixed period during which Tap League ranking and seasonal progression are tracked. Season expiry 
resets temporary Tap Efficiency and starts a new seasonal leaderboard. Keep season configuration in the database. 
Season data Required fields 
Identity seasonId, name, status 
Timing startAt, endAt 
Rewards reward configuration by rank/tier 
Economy tap efficiency rules and seasonal limits 
Leaderboard season-specific accepted tap score 
 
22. Tap League — Reference Analysis 
The uploaded reference screenshots show a competitive leaderboard with a clear rank column, player identity area, 
large central score column, highlighted top ranks, and a persistent 'My Rank' row at the bottom. The important UX 
patterns to reproduce are: 
 Top 100 users are visible in the Tap League. 
 Ranks 1, 2 and 3 should have visually distinct premium rank treatments. 
 Each row should contain rank, avatar/profile image, display name and Tap Score. 
 The current user's row remains pinned/sticky at the bottom even when the user is not in the visible top 100. 
 If the current user is inside the top 100, still keep the 'My Rank' presentation consistent and avoid duplicate 
confusing rows. 
 Use a season indicator and time remaining so users understand when rankings reset. 
 Leaderboard must be server-generated and paginated/limited to the top 100 plus the current user's rank. 
 Do not load an unbounded leaderboard into the browser.

24. Tap & Earn Main Screen 
The supplied Tap & Earn concept contains a top information area, energy card, tap multiplier, boost timer, large central 
tap circle, shortcut cards and bottom navigation. Preserve the information hierarchy but redesign it into a polished 
VELoop fintech interface. 
Zone Must show 
Top user card Avatar/name, level and progress. 
Balance Current VE balance with compact navigation to wallet. 
Energy card 
Current energy/max energy, recharge rate and next 
recharge timer. 
Multiplier Current Multitap and Tap Efficiency states. 
Boost Active/inactive 30-second boost and remaining time. 
Central tap area 
VE coin, tap feedback, combo/streak indicators and 
subtle background motion. 
Feature shortcuts 
Daily Challenge, Missions, Lucky/Spin, Energy Bank, 
upgrades and League where appropriate. 
Bottom nav 
Home, Tap & Earn, Mine, Wallet, Profile consistent with 
the existing VELoop platform. 
 
25. Visual Design System 
Element Direction 
Base #161827

misleading reward claims. 
 
The design should be addictive in the sense of being engaging and rewarding, not visually noisy. Avoid excessive neon, 
giant glows, dozens of floating objects, or casino-like effects. 
26. Frontend Technical Requirements 
 React.js with reusable components and clear feature modules. 
 Use a proper state/data-fetching approach; do not keep authoritative economic values only in local state. 
 Responsive layout for desktop and mobile. 

 Use CSS modules or the project's existing styling convention consistently. 
 Build reusable components for RewardToast, TapButton, EnergyBar, Countdown, BoostCard, UpgradeModal, 
MissionCard, SpinModal, LeagueRow and StickyMyRank. 
 Implement loading, empty, error and retry states. 
 Use optimistic animation only; never optimistically add authoritative currency to the balance. 
 Synchronize server responses after tap batches or state-changing actions. 
 Use accessible buttons, labels, focus states and readable contrast. 
 Prevent accidental double submissions on purchase/claim/spin actions. 
27. Backend Technical Requirements 
 Node.js + Express.js REST API. 
 MongoDB with Mongoose. 
 Authentication must use the existing VELoop authentication mechanism; do not create a second unrelated auth 
system. 
 Server-side tap validation and reward selection. 
 Server-side energy regeneration from timestamps. 
 Server-side upgrade expiry. 
 Server-side daily/season reset logic. 
 Server-side reward ledger for auditability. 
 Atomic balance updates for currencies and reward claims. 
 Idempotency for spin, mission claim, daily challenge claim and purchase operations. 
 Rate limiting and suspicious-tap detection. 
 Centralized configuration for reward probabilities, ranges, cooldowns and season settings. 
 Do not trust client-provided reward amounts, energy amounts, tap score or rank.

30. Tap API Validation Logic 
A valid tap should conceptually follow this sequence: 
1. Authenticate the user. 
2. Generate or validate a unique requestId. 
3. Read current TapState using an atomic/transaction-safe approach. 
4. Regenerate energy from elapsed time. 
5. Check whether the request is too close to the user's last accepted tap. 
6. Reject suspicious/impossible request patterns. 
7. Check available energy and active shield. 
8. Apply efficiency/multitap/boost rules according to current server state. 
9. Select reward using server-side probability configuration. 
10. Update currency/energy/tap counters and season score atomically. 
11. Write RewardLedger and TapEvent. 
12. Return the authoritative new state and reward animation payload. 
31. Anti-Auto-Clicker / Abuse Protection 
 200 ms minimum accepted-tap interval. 
 Server-side timestamp comparison; client timers are not trusted. 

 Rate limiting per user/IP/device as appropriate. 
 Detect impossible sustained patterns, repeated identical request timing and burst anomalies. 
 Use request IDs/idempotency to prevent replaying a tap request. 
 Do not accept a client-supplied reward amount. 
 Do not accept a client-supplied energy deduction. 
 Log suspicious activity for later review. 
 Do not block legitimate mobile users simply because their network latency varies; keep detection threshold 
practical and server-configurable. 
32. Ad Integration Boundary 
The Tap & Earn system should be ad-ready, but ad rendering must not be allowed to manipulate the economy directly 
from the client. Ad completion should be verified through the platform's approved ad/verification flow before granting 
any rewarded benefit. 
 Keep ad placements modular so interstitial, banner and rewarded-video providers can be changed later. 
 Do not hard-code an ad network SDK throughout the TapButton component. 
 Rewarded ad benefits should be explicit: e.g. energy recovery, boost activation or another configured benefit. 
 Maintain an AdEvent record for eligible rewarded actions. 
 Do not grant an economic reward solely because the frontend says an ad finished. 
33. Economy Safety Rules 
 Every upgrade is an economic sink; pricing must be configurable. 
 Temporary multipliers/efficiency must expire and never become permanent accidentally. 
 Season resets must not delete historical ledger data. 
 Reward probabilities must be configurable without redeploying React. 
 Daily/seasonal caps may be introduced from backend configuration if analytics show excessive issuance. 
 All balance-changing operations must be auditable through RewardLedger. 
 The system must support changing SVE/VE/Token ranges later without rewriting the tap UI. 
34. User Experience Rules 
 A new user should understand Energy, Tap, current reward, Multitap, Boost and Season within the first screen. 
 Advanced systems such as Energy Bank, Shield, Efficiency and Fragments should be discoverable but not 
overwhelm the main tap interaction. 
 Every purchase modal must show cost, benefit, duration and expiry in plain language. 
 Every temporary feature must show an expiry countdown. 
 Reward feedback should be immediate and visually lightweight. 
 Use consistent terminology: VE, SVE, Tokens, Gems, Spin, Energy, Tap Efficiency, Tap League, Tap Season. 
35. Acceptance Criteria 
 User can open Tap & Earn and receive complete current state from backend. 
 User can tap the central circle and see animation + haptic feedback where supported. 
 Accepted taps cannot occur faster than the configured server interval. 
 Energy is consumed correctly and regenerated from timestamps. 
 All reward outcomes follow backend-configured probabilities and ranges. 
 VE, SVE, Tokens, Gems and Spin balances are persisted in MongoDB. 

 Multitap, recharge speed, energy capacity and efficiency upgrades work and expire correctly. 
 Boost lasts 30 seconds and displays a synchronized countdown. 
 Energy Shield lasts 10 seconds and correctly prevents eligible energy consumption. 
 Energy Bank lasts exactly 3 days according to server timestamps. 
 Lucky Tap cannot be eligible before 300 accepted taps and spin results cannot be duplicated. 
 Missions and Daily Tap Challenge track progress server-side and can only be claimed once. 
 VE Fragments are stored and displayed as a separate resource. 
 Tap Season is persisted with start/end timestamps and controls seasonal expiry. 
 Tap League displays top 100 and keeps the current user's rank visible at the bottom. 
 Top 3 receive distinct visual treatment. 
 Leaderboard ranking is based on accepted server-side taps for the active season. 
 All currency-changing actions create auditable ledger entries. 
 Refresh/relogin does not reset any progress. 
 Frontend cannot directly manipulate authoritative balances. 
 Responsive UI works without horizontal overflow on mobile. 
 Loading/error/empty states are implemented. 
 No feature is left as a fake button or static placeholder.

40. Final Instruction to Intern 
Do not treat this as a UI-only assignment. The expected result is a working full-stack Tap & Earn system. The UI should 
look polished enough for a product demo, while the backend must be strong enough that a user cannot simply edit 
JavaScript, send a fake reward amount, replay requests or refresh the page to generate currency. Build the feature in a 
modular way because VELoop will tune reward probabilities, costs, seasons and limits after launch.

41. Exact Economy Configuration — Final Locked Requirements 
This section resolves the remaining implementation ambiguities. These are the initial VELoop Tap & Earn values. Every 
numeric value must have one authoritative configuration source and must be referenced everywhere else. 
41.1 Centralized Configuration Rule 
 Create one authoritative Tap & Earn economy/configuration service or database-backed configuration document. 
 All prices, probabilities, reward ranges, cooldowns, durations, thresholds, limits, season rules and ad rules must be 
defined there. 
 Frontend must receive display configuration from the backend; it must not hard-code economic values. 
 Backend services must read the same configuration source rather than repeating numbers in controllers. 
 Admin changes must update the centralized value and all consuming APIs/UI must reflect the change without 
source-code edits. 
 Record every admin configuration change with admin, key, old value, new value, timestamp and reason. 
 Version configuration so historical TapEvent and RewardLedger records remain interpretable. 
41.2 Tap Reward Roll 
Every accepted physical tap performs exactly one server-side reward probability roll. 
Outcome Probability Initial reward 
SVE 60% 1 SVE 
VE 20% Random 0.6–1.7 VE, exactly one digit 
after decimal 
Spin 2% 1 Spin 
Gems 5% Configured values 0.5 / 0.8 / 1.0 / 1.2 
/ up to 2 
Tokens 13% Random 5–100 Tokens 
 
For ranged decimal rewards, use one decimal place only. Prefer configurable weighted discrete values (for example 0.6, 
0.7 ... 1.7) rather than unrestricted floating-point randomness. 
41.3 Physical Tap / Multitap Rule 
One physical tap is one interaction. Multitap changes the effective tap count and energy consumption: x2 means one 
physical tap counts as 2 effective taps and consumes 2 Energy; x3 counts as 3 and consumes 3 Energy. 
 Store both physicalTapCount and effectiveTapCount. 
 Tap League score uses effective accepted taps. 
 Energy consumption equals effective tap count unless the active Energy Shield protects part of the tap. 
 One physical tap performs one reward probability roll; configured Multitap/Efficiency/Boost modifiers are then 
applied according to the centralized economy rules. 
 TapEvent must record the physical count, effective count, energy consumed and final reward.

Tie-breaker: higher effective accepted tap score ranks first; if scores are equal, the user who reached that score earlier 
ranks first; if still equal, use a deterministic database identifier. 
Season rollover: freeze scoring → calculate ranks → distribute rewards exactly once → archive the season → activate the 
next season → reset seasonal efficiency. Historical leaderboard and reward ledger data must remain available. 

42. Ad System — Required Demo Implementation 
Build a modular demo ad system. The admin controls the tap window in which an ad opportunity can appear, with the 
initial range set to 15–40 accepted/effective taps. 
 Central configuration keys: minAdTapThreshold = 15 and maxAdTapThreshold = 40. 
 Use randomized opportunity timing inside the configured range and apply sensible frequency caps. 
 Create a replaceable DemoAdProvider abstraction. 
 Support demo Interstitial, Full-page/Video and Banner placements. 
 Demo ads must be clearly marked as demo/non-production. 
 Do not put ad-network SDK logic inside TapCircle/TapButton. 
 Track opportunity, shown, completed, skipped, failed and rewarded events. 
 Rewarded-ad completion must be verified by a trusted callback/server mechanism before granting an economic 
benefit. 
 Changing the centralized ad configuration must update every consuming UI/API. 
43. Admin Control Center — Admin-Proof Architecture 
The existing VELoop Admin Dashboard must be able to monitor and configure the entire Tap & Earn system. Build a 
dedicated Tap & Earn admin module or expose a clean admin API for the existing dashboard. 
Admin area Monitor/configure 
Economy Config Probabilities, reward values/ranges, prices, multipliers, 
durations, thresholds and limits 
Tap Analytics Physical taps, effective taps, accepted/rejected taps, 
active tappers, taps per hour/day 
Rewards SVE/VE/Token/Gem/Spin issuance and distribution 
Energy Consumption, recharge, capacity upgrades, Bank and 
Shield usage 
Upgrades Purchases, active/expired upgrades and sink totals 
Ads Opportunities, impressions, completion/failure and 
placement performance 
Anti-Bot Rejected taps, rate violations, suspicious patterns and 
risk flags 
Tap League Current season, top 100, score distribution and reward 
status 
Seasons Start/end, active status, rollover/finalization 
Reward Ledger Searchable user/system balance changes 
Config Audit Admin, changed key, old value, new value, timestamp, 
reason 
 
No economic value may be duplicated across files. Admin edits must validate, persist, audit and propagate through the 
same configuration source. 
44. UI/UX — HIGHEST PRIORITY 
The UI is the highest-priority part of this assignment because the user experiences Tap & Earn almost entirely through 
the interface. The intern must treat visual quality, interaction feedback, responsiveness and clarity as functional 
requirements. 
 First viewport must clearly communicate VE balance, Energy, recharge countdown, Multitap, Tap Efficiency, Boost 
and the central Tap Circle. 

 Central Tap Circle is the hero interaction and must feel physically responsive on every accepted tap. 
 Every tap: press/compression animation + ripple/glow + reward float + subtle haptic feedback where supported. 
 Use the supplied VE tap-circle concept as interaction inspiration while using VELoop's own #161827 fintech design 
language. 
 Use VE gold as the primary reward accent and blue as a secondary interaction accent. 
 Do not make every card glow. Reserve stronger effects for active rewards, boosts, Lucky/Mystery events and the 
Tap Circle. 
 Use bottom sheets, drawers and focused modals for advanced systems so the first screen stays understandable. 
 Every purchase must show cost, benefit, duration and expiry before confirmation. 
 Every temporary feature must have a live countdown. 
 Use consistent visual identity for SVE, VE, Tokens, Gems, Spins and Energy. 
 Show a compact last-reward/history feedback area without forcing the user away from the tap screen. 
 Loading, error, rejected tap, reconnecting and empty states must be designed—not plain text placeholders. 
 Never freeze the Tap Circle while waiting for a network response; animate immediately and reconcile with 
authoritative server state. 
 Rejected taps should show subtle reasons such as Too Fast, Not Enough Energy or Cooldown Active. 
 Touch targets must be mobile-friendly and the Tap Circle must not conflict with bottom navigation. 
 Respect reduced-motion preferences where practical. 
 Avoid casino-like effects, excessive particles, flashing, giant gradients or visual clutter. Target: engaging fintech, not 
cheap game UI. 
44.1 First-View Information Hierarchy 
Priority Information 
1 Tap Circle + current reward feedback 
2 Energy current/max + recharge countdown 
3 VE balance + level 
4 Multitap + Tap Efficiency 
5 Boost + countdown 
6 Daily Challenge + Missions 
7 Lucky/Spin + Energy Bank + Shield 
8 VE Fragments + Tap Season 
9 Tap League 
 
44.2 Tap Feedback Sequence 
1. User touches Tap Circle. 
2. Frontend immediately plays press animation and vibration where supported. 
3. Frontend begins the 200 ms interaction lock. 
4. Unique requestId is sent to backend. 
5. Backend validates authentication, timing, energy, Shield, anti-bot and season state. 
6. Backend performs one reward roll and applies configured Multitap/Efficiency/Boost rules. 
7. Backend atomically updates state and writes TapEvent + RewardLedger. 
8. Frontend receives authoritative response. 
9. Reward float displays exactly what was awarded. 
10. Balance, Energy, Combo, Streak and League progress animate to the returned state. 

45. Single-Source Configuration Architecture 
All values below are examples of configuration keys, not duplicated constants. The intern must implement a single 
source of truth. 
 tapEconomy.reward.sve 
 tapEconomy.reward.ve 
 tapEconomy.reward.tokens 
 tapEconomy.reward.gems 
 tapEconomy.reward.spin 
 tapEconomy.energy.baseCapacity 
 tapEconomy.energy.recharge 
 tapEconomy.energy.capacityTiers 
 tapEconomy.multitap.tiers 
 tapEconomy.rechargeSpeed.tiers 
 tapEconomy.energyBank 
 tapEconomy.energyShield 
 tapEconomy.tapEfficiency.tiers 
 tapEconomy.tapStreak 
 tapEconomy.tapCombo 
 tapEconomy.mysteryTap 
 tapEconomy.luckyTap.spinRewards 
 tapEconomy.ads 
 tapEconomy.seasons 
 tapEconomy.league.rewards 
 tapEconomy.security 
46. Reliability, Precision and Concurrency 
 Use integer smallest currency units or MongoDB Decimal128 for fractional balances; never rely on binary floating-
point arithmetic for authoritative balances. 
 Use unique indexes for userId/requestId where replay protection requires them. 
 Index TapEvent by userId + timestamp and seasonId + timestamp/score as appropriate. 
 Tap processing must be atomic so simultaneous requests cannot double-spend Energy or double-award rewards. 
 Configuration changes must not alter historical ledger events. 
 Store timestamps in UTC; convert to local time only in the UI. 
 Server time is authoritative for all cooldowns, recharge, expiry and seasons. 
 State-changing endpoints should return authoritative resulting state or a version number for safe frontend 
reconciliation. 
47. Final UI Acceptance Checklist 
 Premium, attractive first load; no generic template appearance. 
 Tap Circle is dominant but does not hide important information. 
 Tap feedback is visible immediately. 
 Reward types are understandable at a glance. 
 Energy and recharge state are instantly understandable. 
 Multitap, Efficiency and Boost are visually distinct. 
 Temporary features communicate expiry. 
 Ads do not cause layout jumps or destroy the core interaction. 

 Tap League feels competitive and polished with Top 3 and sticky My Rank. 
 Mobile has no horizontal scrolling and controls are thumb-friendly. 
 Desktop uses space naturally without oversized stretched cards. 
 Loading, network failure, rejected tap and success states are designed. 
 Animations are smooth, short and purposeful. 
 The interface remains readable when multiple effects are active. 
 Every visible economy value comes from backend state/configuration. 
48. Final Definition of Done 
The feature is complete only when an authenticated user can tap, consume Energy, receive server-selected rewards, 
purchase and expire upgrades, use Boost/Bank/Shield/Efficiency, complete Missions and Daily Challenges, trigger 
Mystery/Lucky mechanics, accumulate seasonal Tap League score, see Top 100 + My Rank, encounter the configurable 
demo ad system, and have every economic event visible/auditable from the Admin Dashboard. The UI must be polished, 
responsive, engaging and production-facing—not an intern prototype.

VELoop Rewards 
Tap & Earn — Complete MERN Full-Stack 
Intern Task 
Production-oriented implementation specification 
 
Project VELoop Rewards — Tap & Earn 
Stack MERN: MongoDB + Express.js + React.js + Node.js 
Platform body color #161827 
Primary visual direction Minimal • Premium • Fintech • Interactive • Trusted 
Reference 
Uploaded Tap & Earn concept + uploaded Tap League 
screenshots 
Primary objective 
Build the complete frontend + backend, not a static UI 
demo 
 
1. Task Objective 
Build the complete VELoop Rewards Tap & Earn module as a production-style MERN feature. The experience must feel 
engaging like a modern tap-to-earn game, but the visual language must remain premium, minimal, trustworthy and 
fintech-oriented. The implementation must include real backend state, server-authoritative reward calculation, secure 
tap processing, upgrade systems, seasonal progression, Tap League ranking, reward history and all required UI 
interactions. 
2. Non-Negotiable Requirements 
 Use MERN stack throughout the feature. 
 Frontend must be React.js and responsive for desktop and mobile. 
 Backend must be Node.js + Express.js with MongoDB persistence. 
 Do not hard-code balances, energy, rank, reward history, upgrades or season data in React. 
 Backend is the source of truth for rewards, balances, energy, cooldowns, upgrades and leaderboard scores. 
 Every accepted tap must respect a 200 ms minimum processing interval. Frontend must visibly animate every tap 
and provide vibration feedback where supported. 
 The 200 ms delay must NOT be the only anti-bot mechanism. Backend must reject impossible tap rates and 
suspicious sequences. 
 The UI must never feel cluttered. Advanced features should be understandable at first glance and expandable 
through drawers/modals. 
 Use the supplied Tap & Earn visual concept as the structural inspiration, but do not copy another game's branding 
or assets. 
 Use the platform body color #161827 as the foundation of the design system. 
3. Core Tap Interaction 
The central interaction is the VE coin/tap circle. Every tap must feel responsive even though reward processing is 
controlled by the backend. 

Requirement Implementation 
Tap animation 
Scale/press effect, glow/ripple, small coin/token burst 
and subtle counter animation. 
Haptic feedback 
Use navigator.vibrate where supported; fail silently on 
unsupported devices. 
200 ms interval 
Do not accept another tap event locally until the 200 ms 
interaction window is respected. 
Server authority 
Client sends tap request; server validates state and 
decides reward. 
Reward feedback 
Show a compact floating reward such as +1 SVE, +1.2 VE, 
+25 Tokens or +1 Spin. 
No guaranteed reward per tap 
The tap animation happens on every accepted tap, but 
reward outcomes follow configured reward probabilities. 
Low-latency feel 
Animate immediately; reconcile balance/energy with the 
server response. 
Failed tap 
Show subtle feedback such as 'Too fast' or 'Energy 
empty' without a disruptive modal. 
 
4. Tap Reward Distribution 
Use the following initial reward distribution. These values must be configurable from the backend so the economy can 
be tuned later without changing frontend code. 
Outcome Initial probability Reward range / rule 
SVE 60% 
1 SVE per rewarded SVE outcome 
(initial configuration) 
VE 20% 0.6 to 1.7 VE 
Spin 2% 
1 spin whenever a spin outcome is 
selected 
Gems 5% 0.5, 0.8, 1, 1.2, up to 2 gems 
Tokens 13% remainder 5 to 100 tokens 
 
Important: the listed percentages total 87% before the token remainder. Therefore the backend should define Tokens 
as the remaining 13% so the distribution totals exactly 100%. Do not create an unaccounted reward bucket. 
Reward probabilities must be server-side configuration. The client must never decide whether a tap gives SVE, VE, Spin, 
Gems or Tokens. 
5. Energy System 
Feature Requirement 
Base energy 500 / 500 
Consumption 
1 energy per accepted tap before any efficiency rules are 
applied. 
Recharge +20 energy every 20 minutes by default. 
Storage upgrade User can increase maximum capacity by spending VEs. 
Recharge-speed upgrade 
User can increase recharge speed using the designated 
upgrade currency/tokens. 
Zero energy 
Disable accepted taps until energy becomes available or 
the user uses an eligible recovery option. 
Server calculation 
Energy regeneration must be calculated from 
timestamps rather than requiring a request every 20 
minutes. 

Cap 
Regenerated energy can never exceed maximum storage 
capacity. 
 
6. Energy Storage Capacity 
Default capacity is 500. Users can purchase higher capacity. The exact pricing curve should be configurable. Upgrade 
prices must increase faster than capacity so users cannot create uncontrolled reward inflation. 
Suggested initial progression: 500 → 600 → 700 → 800 → 900 → 1000. Keep the values configurable. 
7. Multitap 
Multitap increases the reward value of an accepted physical tap. Default is x1. Users may upgrade up to x3. The upgrade 
is temporary and remains valid for 7 days from activation/purchase. 
Level Tap effect Validity 
x1 1x Default 
x2 2x 7 days 
x3 3x 7 days 
 
The backend must store activation time and expiry time. After expiry, the user automatically falls back to the highest 
non-expired multiplier. 
8. Recharge Speed 
Users can upgrade energy recharge speed. Keep the upgrade curve configurable. Do not allow recharge speed to 
become unlimited. Suggested initial display: +20/20m → +22/20m → +24/20m → +27/20m → +30/20m. 
9. Tap Streak 
Show the user's current consecutive tap streak. The streak is primarily an engagement mechanic. Use a visible counter 
and a lightweight progress effect. Do not make streak rewards large enough to damage the economy. 
10. Precision Tap 
Occasionally display a small precision target during the tap interaction. A user who taps the target accurately receives 
Tokens. The reward amount should be configured by the backend. Precision taps must not bypass normal energy or 
server validation. 
11. Mystery Tap 
A mystery tap is a special tap outcome that awards SVEs. It should be visually distinct but not excessively flashy. The 
backend decides when the event is available and the reward amount. 

12. Tap Combo 
Tap Combo is an animation/engagement layer. It should visually show the user that they are tapping continuously, for 
example COMBO x12, COMBO x25, COMBO x50. The combo animation itself does not need to create a separate 
economic reward unless explicitly enabled later. 
13. Boost Windows 
Provide a temporary 30-second boost window. The boost may increase the tap reward according to backend 
configuration. It should have a clear countdown, active state and expiry animation. Boost activation must be logged. 
14. Lucky Tap + Spin 
Lucky Tap cannot trigger before the user reaches a minimum of 300 accepted taps in the relevant tracking window. 
After 300 taps, the backend may randomly trigger a Lucky Tap. The reward interaction is a Spin. 
 Show a clear progress indicator toward the 300-tap threshold. 
 Before 300 taps, do not display a misleading 'almost lucky' state that implies a guaranteed reward. 
 After eligibility, the backend controls the trigger. 
 Spin result must be server-generated and recorded in reward history. 
 Prevent double-spinning through idempotent server-side processing. 
15. Tap Missions 
Create daily/seasonal missions that award Tokens. Examples: 
 Complete 100 accepted taps. 
 Complete 500 accepted taps. 
 Reach a target combo. 
 Complete a precision tap. 
 Use a boost window. 
 Return and tap on multiple sessions. 
16. Daily Tap Challenge 
Create a daily challenge with convenient, controlled rewards. The user should see progress immediately. The challenge 
resets according to the platform's daily reset time. Backend must enforce completion and prevent duplicate claims. 
17. Energy Bank 
Users can purchase an Energy Bank valid for 3 days. The Energy Bank is a separate temporary energy reserve. The exact 
capacity and price should be configurable. The UI must clearly show its expiry countdown and remaining capacity. 
18. Energy Shield 
Users can purchase/activate an Energy Shield using SVEs. Shield duration is 10 seconds. During the active window, 
eligible taps do not consume energy. The shield must have a visible countdown and server-side start/expiry 
timestamps. 

19. Tap Efficiency 
Tap Efficiency is a temporary seasonal/monthly upgrade. Initial levels: 1.1x, 1.2x and 1.3x. The user's purchased 
efficiency expires when the current Tap Season expires. Do not make it permanent. 
The frontend must show the current efficiency, current level, upgrade cost and exact expiry date/time. 
20. VE Fragments 
Introduce VE Fragments as a separate collectible/progression resource. The conversion/value will remain configurable 
and can be decided later. Build the data model and UI so the value can change without a database migration. 
21. Tap Seasons 
A Tap Season is a fixed period during which Tap League ranking and seasonal progression are tracked. Season expiry 
resets temporary Tap Efficiency and starts a new seasonal leaderboard. Keep season configuration in the database. 
Season data Required fields 
Identity seasonId, name, status 
Timing startAt, endAt 
Rewards reward configuration by rank/tier 
Economy tap efficiency rules and seasonal limits 
Leaderboard season-specific accepted tap score 
 
22. Tap League — Reference Analysis 
The uploaded reference screenshots show a competitive leaderboard with a clear rank column, player identity area, 
large central score column, highlighted top ranks, and a persistent 'My Rank' row at the bottom. The important UX 
patterns to reproduce are: 
 Top 100 users are visible in the Tap League. 
 Ranks 1, 2 and 3 should have visually distinct premium rank treatments. 
 Each row should contain rank, avatar/profile image, display name and Tap Score. 
 The current user's row remains pinned/sticky at the bottom even when the user is not in the visible top 100. 
 If the current user is inside the top 100, still keep the 'My Rank' presentation consistent and avoid duplicate 
confusing rows. 
 Use a season indicator and time remaining so users understand when rankings reset. 
 Leaderboard must be server-generated and paginated/limited to the top 100 plus the current user's rank. 
 Do not load an unbounded leaderboard into the browser. 
23. Tap League UI Layout 
Area UI requirement 
Header 
Tap League title, current season name, season 
countdown. 
Top 3 
Special rank cards/rows for #1, #2, #3 with premium but 
restrained visual treatment. 
Rows 4–100 
Compact leaderboard rows with rank, avatar, username 
and total accepted taps. 
My Rank 
Sticky bottom row with highlighted border/background 
and current user's rank/score. 

Empty/loading Skeleton rows; no layout jump. 
Reward preview Show what top ranks receive at season end. 
Mobile 
Keep rank and score readable without horizontal 
scrolling. 
 
24. Tap & Earn Main Screen 
The supplied Tap & Earn concept contains a top information area, energy card, tap multiplier, boost timer, large central 
tap circle, shortcut cards and bottom navigation. Preserve the information hierarchy but redesign it into a polished 
VELoop fintech interface. 
Zone Must show 
Top user card Avatar/name, level and progress. 
Balance Current VE balance with compact navigation to wallet. 
Energy card 
Current energy/max energy, recharge rate and next 
recharge timer. 
Multiplier Current Multitap and Tap Efficiency states. 
Boost Active/inactive 30-second boost and remaining time. 
Central tap area 
VE coin, tap feedback, combo/streak indicators and 
subtle background motion. 
Feature shortcuts 
Daily Challenge, Missions, Lucky/Spin, Energy Bank, 
upgrades and League where appropriate. 
Bottom nav 
Home, Tap & Earn, Mine, Wallet, Profile consistent with 
the existing VELoop platform. 
 
25. Visual Design System 
Element Direction 
Base #161827 
Primary accent 
Warm VE gold/yellow; use sparingly for value/reward 
states. 
Secondary accent Electric blue for active/interactive states. 
Cards 
Deep navy/blue-black surfaces, subtle border, low-
opacity glow. 
Typography 
Modern sans-serif such as Inter/Manrope; clear 
hierarchy. 
Corners Moderately rounded, not oversized/puffy. 
Motion 
Short, purposeful transitions; avoid constant particle 
overload. 
Trust 
Clear labels, predictable controls, readable values and no 
misleading reward claims. 
 
The design should be addictive in the sense of being engaging and rewarding, not visually noisy. Avoid excessive neon, 
giant glows, dozens of floating objects, or casino-like effects. 
26. Frontend Technical Requirements 
 React.js with reusable components and clear feature modules. 
 Use a proper state/data-fetching approach; do not keep authoritative economic values only in local state. 
 Responsive layout for desktop and mobile. 

 Use CSS modules or the project's existing styling convention consistently. 
 Build reusable components for RewardToast, TapButton, EnergyBar, Countdown, BoostCard, UpgradeModal, 
MissionCard, SpinModal, LeagueRow and StickyMyRank. 
 Implement loading, empty, error and retry states. 
 Use optimistic animation only; never optimistically add authoritative currency to the balance. 
 Synchronize server responses after tap batches or state-changing actions. 
 Use accessible buttons, labels, focus states and readable contrast. 
 Prevent accidental double submissions on purchase/claim/spin actions. 
27. Backend Technical Requirements 
 Node.js + Express.js REST API. 
 MongoDB with Mongoose. 
 Authentication must use the existing VELoop authentication mechanism; do not create a second unrelated auth 
system. 
 Server-side tap validation and reward selection. 
 Server-side energy regeneration from timestamps. 
 Server-side upgrade expiry. 
 Server-side daily/season reset logic. 
 Server-side reward ledger for auditability. 
 Atomic balance updates for currencies and reward claims. 
 Idempotency for spin, mission claim, daily challenge claim and purchase operations. 
 Rate limiting and suspicious-tap detection. 
 Centralized configuration for reward probabilities, ranges, cooldowns and season settings. 
 Do not trust client-provided reward amounts, energy amounts, tap score or rank. 
28. Suggested MongoDB Models 
Collection Important fields 
User 
profile, level, balances, gems, tokens, spins, 
currentTapSeasonId 
TapState 
userId, energy, maxEnergy, rechargeRate, lastEnergyAt, 
tapMultiplier, multiplierExpiresAt, efficiency, 
efficiencyExpiresAt, streak, combo 
TapEvent 
userId, seasonId, timestamp, serverAcceptedAt, 
rewardType, rewardAmount, energyBefore, energyAfter, 
requestId 
Upgrade userId, type, level, cost, purchasedAt, expiresAt 
Boost userId, type, startedAt, expiresAt, status 
Mission 
missionId, seasonId, type, target, reward, activeFrom, 
activeTo 
UserMission userId, missionId, progress, completed, claimedAt 
Spin 
userId, seasonId, spinId, eligibleAt, resultType, 
resultAmount, createdAt 
TapSeason 
name, startAt, endAt, status, efficiencyRules, 
rewardRules 
TapLeagueScore seasonId, userId, acceptedTapCount, updatedAt 
RewardLedger 
userId, source, type, amount, currency, referenceId, 
createdAt 
AdEvent 
userId, placement, provider, eventType, createdAt, 
optionalRewardReference 
 

29. Suggested API Surface 
Method Endpoint Purpose 
GET /api/tap/state 
Return complete current Tap & Earn 
state. 
POST /api/tap 
Validate and process one accepted 
tap. 
GET /api/tap/history Return recent reward/tap history. 
POST /api/tap/boost/activate Activate eligible 30-second boost. 
POST /api/tap/energy-bank/purchase Purchase 3-day Energy Bank. 
POST /api/tap/shield/purchase 
Purchase/activate 10-second Energy 
Shield. 
POST /api/tap/upgrade Purchase an eligible upgrade. 
GET /api/tap/missions Return active missions and progress. 
POST /api/tap/missions/:id/claim Claim completed mission reward. 
GET /api/tap/daily-challenge Return today's challenge. 
POST /api/tap/daily-challenge/claim Claim completed daily challenge. 
GET /api/tap/lucky Return Lucky Tap eligibility/status. 
POST /api/tap/lucky/spin 
Execute one server-authoritative 
spin. 
GET /api/tap/league Return top 100 + current user's rank. 
GET /api/tap/season Return active season and countdown. 
 
30. Tap API Validation Logic 
A valid tap should conceptually follow this sequence: 
1. Authenticate the user. 
2. Generate or validate a unique requestId. 
3. Read current TapState using an atomic/transaction-safe approach. 
4. Regenerate energy from elapsed time. 
5. Check whether the request is too close to the user's last accepted tap. 
6. Reject suspicious/impossible request patterns. 
7. Check available energy and active shield. 
8. Apply efficiency/multitap/boost rules according to current server state. 
9. Select reward using server-side probability configuration. 
10. Update currency/energy/tap counters and season score atomically. 
11. Write RewardLedger and TapEvent. 
12. Return the authoritative new state and reward animation payload. 
31. Anti-Auto-Clicker / Abuse Protection 
 200 ms minimum accepted-tap interval. 
 Server-side timestamp comparison; client timers are not trusted. 

 Rate limiting per user/IP/device as appropriate. 
 Detect impossible sustained patterns, repeated identical request timing and burst anomalies. 
 Use request IDs/idempotency to prevent replaying a tap request. 
 Do not accept a client-supplied reward amount. 
 Do not accept a client-supplied energy deduction. 
 Log suspicious activity for later review. 
 Do not block legitimate mobile users simply because their network latency varies; keep detection threshold 
practical and server-configurable. 
32. Ad Integration Boundary 
The Tap & Earn system should be ad-ready, but ad rendering must not be allowed to manipulate the economy directly 
from the client. Ad completion should be verified through the platform's approved ad/verification flow before granting 
any rewarded benefit. 
 Keep ad placements modular so interstitial, banner and rewarded-video providers can be changed later. 
 Do not hard-code an ad network SDK throughout the TapButton component. 
 Rewarded ad benefits should be explicit: e.g. energy recovery, boost activation or another configured benefit. 
 Maintain an AdEvent record for eligible rewarded actions. 
 Do not grant an economic reward solely because the frontend says an ad finished. 
33. Economy Safety Rules 
 Every upgrade is an economic sink; pricing must be configurable. 
 Temporary multipliers/efficiency must expire and never become permanent accidentally. 
 Season resets must not delete historical ledger data. 
 Reward probabilities must be configurable without redeploying React. 
 Daily/seasonal caps may be introduced from backend configuration if analytics show excessive issuance. 
 All balance-changing operations must be auditable through RewardLedger. 
 The system must support changing SVE/VE/Token ranges later without rewriting the tap UI. 
34. User Experience Rules 
 A new user should understand Energy, Tap, current reward, Multitap, Boost and Season within the first screen. 
 Advanced systems such as Energy Bank, Shield, Efficiency and Fragments should be discoverable but not 
overwhelm the main tap interaction. 
 Every purchase modal must show cost, benefit, duration and expiry in plain language. 
 Every temporary feature must show an expiry countdown. 
 Reward feedback should be immediate and visually lightweight. 
 Use consistent terminology: VE, SVE, Tokens, Gems, Spin, Energy, Tap Efficiency, Tap League, Tap Season. 
35. Acceptance Criteria 
 User can open Tap & Earn and receive complete current state from backend. 
 User can tap the central circle and see animation + haptic feedback where supported. 
 Accepted taps cannot occur faster than the configured server interval. 
 Energy is consumed correctly and regenerated from timestamps. 
 All reward outcomes follow backend-configured probabilities and ranges. 
 VE, SVE, Tokens, Gems and Spin balances are persisted in MongoDB. 

 Multitap, recharge speed, energy capacity and efficiency upgrades work and expire correctly. 
 Boost lasts 30 seconds and displays a synchronized countdown. 
 Energy Shield lasts 10 seconds and correctly prevents eligible energy consumption. 
 Energy Bank lasts exactly 3 days according to server timestamps. 
 Lucky Tap cannot be eligible before 300 accepted taps and spin results cannot be duplicated. 
 Missions and Daily Tap Challenge track progress server-side and can only be claimed once. 
 VE Fragments are stored and displayed as a separate resource. 
 Tap Season is persisted with start/end timestamps and controls seasonal expiry. 
 Tap League displays top 100 and keeps the current user's rank visible at the bottom. 
 Top 3 receive distinct visual treatment. 
 Leaderboard ranking is based on accepted server-side taps for the active season. 
 All currency-changing actions create auditable ledger entries. 
 Refresh/relogin does not reset any progress. 
 Frontend cannot directly manipulate authoritative balances. 
 Responsive UI works without horizontal overflow on mobile. 
 Loading/error/empty states are implemented. 
 No feature is left as a fake button or static placeholder. 
36. Deliverables From Intern 
 Complete React frontend for Tap & Earn. 
 Complete Node/Express API. 
 MongoDB/Mongoose schemas and indexes. 
 Authentication integration with the existing VELoop user system. 
 Tap processing and anti-abuse implementation. 
 Upgrade, boost, mission, daily challenge, lucky spin, energy bank, shield and season logic. 
 Tap League backend and frontend. 
 Reward ledger/history. 
 Responsive UI matching VELoop's #161827 fintech design direction. 
 Environment variable documentation.

40. Final Instruction to Intern

41. Exact Economy Configuration — Final Locked Requirements 
This section resolves the remaining implementation ambiguities. These are the initial VELoop Tap & Earn values. Every 
numeric value must have one authoritative configuration source and must be referenced everywhere else. 
41.1 Centralized Configuration Rule 
 Create one authoritative Tap & Earn economy/configuration service or database-backed configuration document. 
 All prices, probabilities, reward ranges, cooldowns, durations, thresholds, limits, season rules and ad rules must be 
defined there. 
 Frontend must receive display configuration from the backend; it must not hard-code economic values. 
 Backend services must read the same configuration source rather than repeating numbers in controllers. 
 Admin changes must update the centralized value and all consuming APIs/UI must reflect the change without 
source-code edits. 
 Record every admin configuration change with admin, key, old value, new value, timestamp and reason. 
 Version configuration so historical TapEvent and RewardLedger records remain interpretable. 
41.2 Tap Reward Roll 
Every accepted physical tap performs exactly one server-side reward probability roll. 
Outcome Probability Initial reward 
SVE 60% 1 SVE

after decimal 
Spin 2% 1 Spin 
Gems 5% Configured values 0.5 / 0.8 / 1.0 / 1.2 
/ up to 2 
Tokens 13% Random 5–100 Tokens 
 
For ranged decimal rewards, use one decimal place only. Prefer configurable weighted discrete values (for example 0.6, 
0.7 ... 1.7) rather than unrestricted floating-point randomness. 
41.3 Physical Tap / Multitap Rule 
One physical tap is one interaction. Multitap changes the effective tap count and energy consumption: x2 means one 
physical tap counts as 2 effective taps and consumes 2 Energy; x3 counts as 3 and consumes 3 Energy. 
 Store both physicalTapCount and effectiveTapCount. 
 Tap League score uses effective accepted taps. 
 Energy consumption equals effective tap count unless the active Energy Shield protects part of the tap. 
 One physical tap performs one reward probability roll; configured Multitap/Efficiency/Boost modifiers are then 
applied according to the centralized economy rules. 
 TapEvent must record the physical count, effective count, energy consumed and final reward. 
41.4 Energy Capacity Pricing 
Capacity Cost 
500 → 600 100 VEs 
600 → 700 150 VEs 
700 → 800 210 VEs 
800 → 900 Configurable; must be seeded before production 
900 → 1000 Configurable; must be seeded before production 
 

41.5 Multitap Pricing 
Tier Cost Validity 
x1.0 Default No purchase 
x1.1 1000 SVEs 7 days 
x1.2 1300 SVEs 7 days 
x1.3 Configurable next tier 7 days 
 
Keep the tier list configurable so future tiers can be added without rewriting UI or business logic. 
41.6 Recharge Speed Pricing 
Recharge Interval Cost 
+20 Energy 20 minutes Default 
+22 Energy 20 minutes 2000 Tokens 
Next tiers 20 minutes Configurable 
 
41.7 Energy Bank — Final Rule 
Property Requirement 
Initial capacity 500 Energy 
Purchase #1 100 VEs 
Purchase #2 500 VEs 
Maximum purchases 2 per active 3-day Bank cycle 
Recharge +20 Energy every 120 minutes 
Priority Bank Energy is consumed before normal Energy 
Validity 3 days 
Expiry Remaining Bank Energy is lost 
Stacking No duration stacking; second purchase adds another 500 
Bank Energy capacity, up to 1000 total during the same 
active cycle 
 
Here, stacking means combining active purchases. V1 allows two purchases but does not extend the 3-day expiry. The 
second purchase can increase active Bank capacity from 500 to 1000. 
41.8 Energy Shield — Final Rule 
Property Requirement 
Cost 100 VEs 
Duration 30 seconds 
Protection 90% of eligible taps consume no Energy; 10% consume 
normal Energy 
Minimum Energy required None 
Active shields 1 maximum 
Purchase while active Blocked 
Cooldown after use 5 minutes 
Stacking Not allowed 
 
The server decides the protected/charged tap outcome; the client must never decide which 10% consume Energy. 
41.9 Tap Efficiency — Final Rule 
Efficiency Cost Validity 
x1.0 Default Current season 
x1.1 1.1 SVEs Current Tap Season 
x1.2 1.2 SVEs Current Tap Season 

x1.3 Configurable Current Tap Season 
 
Tap Efficiency expires at season end. Implement its effect as a configurable multiplier on eligible reward amounts, with 
currency-specific rounding. Do not multiply Spins or unrelated outcomes unless explicitly enabled in configuration. 
41.10 Tap Streak vs Tap Combo 
System Purpose Reset 
Tap Streak Longer-term 
engagement/progression 
5 seconds inactivity 
Tap Combo Short rapid-tapping visual effect 2 seconds inactivity 
 
They must use separate state variables and separate reset timers. 
41.11 Mystery Tap 
After every 250 effective taps, the user receives one Mystery Tap eligibility roll. There is a 0.5% chance of triggering the 
Mystery Tap at that milestone. A successful Mystery Tap awards an SVE amount configured by the backend. The 
milestone and attempt are server-tracked. 
41.12 Lucky Tap / Spin Reward Table 
Outcome Probability

500 VEs 0% — disabled, configurable for future 
20 VEs 5% 
2 Spins 10% 
10 Gems 8% 
100 SVEs 12% 
50 SVEs 25% 
Better Luck 10% 
₹5 Amazon Voucher 0% — disabled, configurable for future 
+15 Energy 5% 
 
These probabilities total exactly 100%. The server creates and records the spin result before the client reveals the 
animation result. 
41.13 Tap League Final Rewards 
Rank Season reward 
#1 10,000 VEs + 5 Spins 
#2 5,000 VEs + 3 Spins 
#3 1,500 VEs + 1 Spin 
#4–10 500 VEs + 2,500 Tokens 
#11–25 5,000 SVEs + 1,000 Tokens 
#26–50 2,500 SVEs + 10 Gems 
#51–100 1,000 SVEs + 500 Tokens 
 
Tie-breaker: higher effective accepted tap score ranks first; if scores are equal, the user who reached that score earlier 
ranks first; if still equal, use a deterministic database identifier. 
Season rollover: freeze scoring → calculate ranks → distribute rewards exactly once → archive the season → activate the 
next season → reset seasonal efficiency. Historical leaderboard and reward ledger data must remain available. 

42. Ad System — Required Demo Implementation 
Build a modular demo ad system. The admin controls the tap window in which an ad opportunity can appear, with the 
initial range set to 15–40 accepted/effective taps. 
 Central configuration keys: minAdTapThreshold = 15 and maxAdTapThreshold = 40. 
 Use randomized opportunity timing inside the configured range and apply sensible frequency caps. 
 Create a replaceable DemoAdProvider abstraction. 
 Support demo Interstitial, Full-page/Video and Banner placements. 
 Demo ads must be clearly marked as demo/non-production. 
 Do not put ad-network SDK logic inside TapCircle/TapButton. 
 Track opportunity, shown, completed, skipped, failed and rewarded events. 
 Rewarded-ad completion must be verified by a trusted callback/server mechanism before granting an economic 
benefit. 
 Changing the centralized ad configuration must update every consuming UI/API. 
43. Admin Control Center — Admin-Proof Architecture 
The existing VELoop Admin Dashboard must be able to monitor and configure the entire Tap & Earn system. Build a 
dedicated Tap & Earn admin module or expose a clean admin API for the existing dashboard.

durations, thresholds and limits

active tappers, taps per hour/day

Shield usage

placement performance

risk flags

status

reason 
 
No economic value may be duplicated across files. Admin edits must validate, persist, audit and propagate through the 
same configuration source. 
44. UI/UX — HIGHEST PRIORITY 
The UI is the highest-priority part of this assignment because the user experiences Tap & Earn almost entirely through 
the interface. The intern must treat visual quality, interaction feedback, responsiveness and clarity as functional 
requirements. 
 First viewport must clearly communicate VE balance, Energy, recharge countdown, Multitap, Tap Efficiency, Boost 
and the central Tap Circle. 

 Central Tap Circle is the hero interaction and must feel physically responsive on every accepted tap. 
 Every tap: press/compression animation + ripple/glow + reward float + subtle haptic feedback where supported. 
 Use the supplied VE tap-circle concept as interaction inspiration while using VELoop's own #161827 fintech design 
language. 
 Use VE gold as the primary reward accent and blue as a secondary interaction accent. 
 Do not make every card glow. Reserve stronger effects for active rewards, boosts, Lucky/Mystery events and the 
Tap Circle. 
 Use bottom sheets, drawers and focused modals for advanced systems so the first screen stays understandable. 
 Every purchase must show cost, benefit, duration and expiry before confirmation. 
 Every temporary feature must have a live countdown. 
 Use consistent visual identity for SVE, VE, Tokens, Gems, Spins and Energy. 
 Show a compact last-reward/history feedback area without forcing the user away from the tap screen. 
 Loading, error, rejected tap, reconnecting and empty states must be designed—not plain text placeholders. 
 Never freeze the Tap Circle while waiting for a network response; animate immediately and reconcile with 
authoritative server state. 
 Rejected taps should show subtle reasons such as Too Fast, Not Enough Energy or Cooldown Active. 
 Touch targets must be mobile-friendly and the Tap Circle must not conflict with bottom navigation. 
 Respect reduced-motion preferences where practical. 
 Avoid casino-like effects, excessive particles, flashing, giant gradients or visual clutter. Target: engaging fintech, not 
cheap game UI.

44.2 Tap Feedback Sequence 
1. User touches Tap Circle. 
2. Frontend immediately plays press animation and vibration where supported. 
3. Frontend begins the 200 ms interaction lock. 
4. Unique requestId is sent to backend. 
5. Backend validates authentication, timing, energy, Shield, anti-bot and season state. 
6. Backend performs one reward roll and applies configured Multitap/Efficiency/Boost rules. 
7. Backend atomically updates state and writes TapEvent + RewardLedger. 
8. Frontend receives authoritative response. 
9. Reward float displays exactly what was awarded. 
10. Balance, Energy, Combo, Streak and League progress animate to the returned state. 

45. Single-Source Configuration Architecture 
All values below are examples of configuration keys, not duplicated constants. The intern must implement a single 
source of truth. 
 tapEconomy.reward.sve

 tapEconomy.ads

46. Reliability, Precision and Concurrency 
 Use integer smallest currency units or MongoDB Decimal128 for fractional balances; never rely on binary floating-
point arithmetic for authoritative balances. 
 Use unique indexes for userId/requestId where replay protection requires them. 
 Index TapEvent by userId + timestamp and seasonId + timestamp/score as appropriate. 
 Tap processing must be atomic so simultaneous requests cannot double-spend Energy or double-award rewards. 
 Configuration changes must not alter historical ledger events. 
 Store timestamps in UTC; convert to local time only in the UI. 
 Server time is authoritative for all cooldowns, recharge, expiry and seasons. 
 State-changing endpoints should return authoritative resulting state or a version number for safe frontend 
reconciliation. 
47. Final UI Acceptance Checklist 
 Premium, attractive first load; no generic template appearance. 
 Tap Circle is dominant but does not hide important information. 
 Tap feedback is visible immediately. 
 Reward types are understandable at a glance. 
 Energy and recharge state are instantly understandable. 
 Multitap, Efficiency and Boost are visually distinct. 
 Temporary features communicate expiry. 
 Ads do not cause layout jumps or destroy the core interaction. 

 Tap League feels competitive and polished with Top 3 and sticky My Rank. 
 Mobile has no horizontal scrolling and controls are thumb-friendly. 
 Desktop uses space naturally without oversized stretched cards. 
 Loading, network failure, rejected tap and success states are designed. 
 Animations are smooth, short and purposeful. 
 The interface remains readable when multiple effects are active. 
 Every visible economy value comes from backend state/configuration. 
48. Final Definition of Done 
The feature is complete only when an authenticated user can tap, consume Energy, receive server-selected rewards, 
purchase and expire upgrades, use Boost/Bank/Shield/Efficiency, complete Missions and Daily Challenges, trigger 
Mystery/Lucky mechanics, accumulate seasonal Tap League score, see Top 100 + My Rank, encounter the configurable
